key_claims: Stopping statins in adults 75 and older with no history of heart disease or stroke does not increase the risk of death over three years compared with continuing statins.
In those who stopped statins, 'bad' cholesterol rose around 50%.
The trial was published in The Lancet Healthy Longevity.
limitations: The study only followed participants for three years.
The study focused on adults 75 and older with no history of heart disease or stroke, so results may not apply to other populations.
The source does not provide details on the number of participants or other potential limitations.
what_not_to_say: Stopping statins is safe for all older adults.
Stopping statins has no effect on cholesterol levels.
The study proves that statins are ineffective in older adults.
The study provides evidence on long-term outcomes beyond three years.
